title: kbfacts.parse_tag reads only the first source of [CODE S-a: path; S-b: path], so the second id of such tags is not cited
goal: SP-5x5ut5ko retrospective (ST-owuunsvl's worker): parse_tag drops a part with no kind, so a tag written [CODE S-a: path | S-b: path] with a semicolon between its sources cites S-a only and its second sources have no citation and no anchor; the parser reads each 'S-x: path' part that follows a kinded part as another source of that kind, so every source of such a tag is cited, and kb/_self/content-rules.md names the form

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbfacts;p=kbfacts.parse_tag('[CODE S-sipjyeoi: internal/a.go; S-gfjnysog: internal/b.go]');ids=[i for x in p for i in x['ids']];print('ids parsed:',ids);sys.exit(0 if 'S-gfjnysog' in ids else 1)
import sys;t=open('kb/_self/content-rules.md',encoding='utf-8').read();ok='[CODE S-a: path; S-b: path]' in t;print('content-rules.md names the two-source form:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

notes: Premise run 2026-10-12: the repro prints ids parsed: ['S-sipjyeoi'] on main. Choice made at planning: the parser reads the second source, no article is rewritten (smaller, reversible). Readers outside touches: .claude/skills/kb-verify/lint.py:340 and :149 and _tools/factdiff.py:2059 take parse_tag's parts, so the lint check (check 1) must stay at errors=0 after the change; a CODE pointer error it then shows stops the item with a report, since the lint file guards a rule. Check 2 reads the form named in content-rules.md. Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 2 of 19, "Lookup correctness: router experts, the tag parser and aliases answer what the kb holds"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed. Checks 0 (rag.py eval) and 1 (lint.py) pass before the work: they pin that the parser change breaks no reader.
